main_text.p: Sunt, certè sunt, quemadmodū & ratio docet, & ueteres testātur, gentes aliæ aliis perspicaciores, propter cœli primùm, deinde humorū temperationē: nullius tamē nationis cuncti homines tam stupidi inueniuntur, quín, si excolantur multū, in quauis re cōsequi possint. Attici, aliíq; Græci fere, propter cœli bonitatem, sem per excelleti ingenio habiti sunt: un de & ab eis omnes fermè disciplinæ, quas modò colimus, emanarūt. con tra Bœotij, in crassiore cœlo nati, lo cum dederūt prouerbio, Bœoticum ingeniū: & ut Horat. ait, Bœotū in crasso iurares aere natū: cū tamē ea gens Pindarū & Plutarchū, alterum poetā, eximiū philosophū alterū, & Epaminondā belli ducē præstantissimū dederit. Atq; idem de reliquis gentibus intelligendū est, eo acutiores, atq; ad omnes disciplinas aptiores esse, quo puriore, tēperatioreq; cœlo utantur: stupidiores fere, quo crassiore: nō ob animi uim quidē il-lam,

page.notes: Printed text is clear. Some words in the line-ends are uncertain (e.g. "quauis", "excelleti", "temperationē") and are transcribed as printed. The signature mark at the foot left is partly illegible and is given approximately.
